A note on the base change map for cohomology
Mathematical Institute of the University of Bonn

In general, given a geometrically integral Deligne–Mumford stack \(\mathcal{X}\) of relative dimension \(1\) over a base scheme \(S\) whose generic point has a stabilizer of \(\mu_n\), it follows from work of Abramovich–Olsson–Vistoli [AOV08, Appendix A] that there exists a stack \(\mathcal{X}//\mu_n\) (called the rigidification of \(\mathcal{X}\)) and a factorization \(\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}//\mu_n \to S\) such that \(\pi\) is a \(\mu_n\)-gerbe and the stabilizer of a point of \(\mathcal{X}//\mu_n\) is the quotient by \(\mu_n\) of the stabilizer of the corresponding point of \(\mathcal{X}\). Finally, since \(\pi\) is a gerbe, and in particular étale, this does not affect the sections of the relative sheaf of differentials or the canonical ring.
